haiku-low.q1: The scheduler starts it at 02:00 UTC, or a retry. It extracts replica rows with updated_at greater than the mark minus 2 hours, including soft-deleted rows.
haiku-low.q2: A bulk-import transaction can stay open up to 90 minutes, and updated_at is stamped at write, not commit. So a row can appear up to 90 minutes after its updated_at.
haiku-low.q3: The next nightly extract picks it up through the 2-hour lookback, since its newer updated_at falls in the window. Merge then replaces the stored row because the staged updated_at is greater.
haiku-low.q4: Soft delete sets deleted_at, which also moves updated_at. The merge sets is_deleted to true. The row stays in fact_orders and is never physically removed.
haiku-low.q5: The attempt is marked failed and retried 15 minutes later, up to two more times. After the third failure the scheduler pages on-call, and nothing runs until the next night.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards show the previous committed night. A staleness alert is posted to #data-alerts.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares count and checksum per creation day for the last 30 days, then reloads mismatched days from the replica through the merge.
haiku-low.q8: Merge keeps only the newest staged row per order_id. It replaces a stored row only if the staged updated_at is greater than or equal to the stored one.
haiku-low.q9: In the single etl_watermark row. It is set to the greater of this attempt's new mark and the current mark, during the Merge transaction, on commit.
haiku-low.q10: Merge runs as one warehouse transaction. Upserts and the mark advance commit together or not at all, so dashboards see only the previous committed night until then.
haiku-low.q11: The staged data is discarded, since each attempt empties stg_orders at start. The retry extracts rows with updated_at greater than the same unchanged mark minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads replica rows of all mismatched days into stg_orders, then runs the step 2 merge once. Its new mark is left empty, so it never moves the nightly mark.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts it at 02:00 UTC (or a retry). It extracts replica `orders` rows (including soft-deleted) with `updated_at` greater than the mark minus 2 hours.
sonnet.q2: A bulk-import transaction can stay open up to 90 minutes, and `updated_at` is stamped at write, not commit, so the row can appear up to 90 minutes after its `updated_at`.
sonnet.q3: The edit moves `updated_at`, so the next nightly extract (mark minus 2h lookback) picks up the new version, and Merge upserts it into `fact_orders` (replacing the row since staged `updated_at` is >= stored).
sonnet.q4: Soft delete sets `deleted_at` and moves `updated_at`. It is extracted as a normal change; Merge upserts it and sets `is_deleted` true. The row stays in `fact_orders`; the app never hard-deletes and rows are never physically removed.
sonnet.q5: The scheduler marks the `etl_runs` row failed, kills a hung job, and starts a new attempt 15 min after the failure from Extract with the same mark (max 2 retries, 3 attempts total). After the third failure it pages on-call and nothing runs until the next night. The mark and `fact_orders` are unchanged.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards refresh at 06:00 regardless and show the previous committed night. The 06:00 check posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts.
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares row count and checksum per creation day for the last 30 days between replica and `fact_orders`, reloads the replica rows of mismatched days into staging, and runs the merge.
sonnet.q8: Merge keeps only the row with greatest `updated_at` per `order_id` in staging, and upserts into `fact_orders` replacing an existing row only if the staged `updated_at` >= the stored one. Merge is idempotent.
sonnet.q9: In the single row of the warehouse table `etl_watermark`. The value is the greater of the attempt's new mark (largest `updated_at` it copied, from its `etl_runs` row) and the current mark. It is written inside the Merge transaction, on commit, together with the data load.
sonnet.q10: Merge upserts into `fact_orders` and advances the mark in one warehouse transaction that commits as a whole or not at all.
sonnet.q11: Staging is emptied (truncated) at the start of the retry attempt, and the retry starts from Extract with the same unchanged mark, extracting `updated_at` > mark minus 2 hours.
sonnet.q12: It copies the replica rows of all mismatched creation days (in the last 30) into `stg_orders`, then runs the step 2 merge once (upsert, newest wins). No, its new mark is empty, so it never changes the mark.
